messages:
kevin: Heads up — saw a regression after increasing max_tokens_per_batch for L4 targets. p95 tail doubled on chat workloads after bump to 32k. Anyone else see this?

maria: I noticed a drop too on L4 tests. Throughput went up a bit but latency distribution got worse.

raj: Can you paste the profile flame or kernel selection log? my suspicion: kernel selector picks a slower kernel when batch "token shape" crosses a threshold.

kevin: Putting snippets — profiler shows we moved from `attn_v2_fused` -> `attn_generic` for mid-length sequences. Also seeing more frequent KV flushes.

kevin: ```
[profile] batch_tokens=32768 model=gptx-l4 kernel=attn_generic latency_ms=8.2
[profile] batch_tokens=16384 model=gptx-l4 kernel=attn_v2_fused latency_ms=4.1
GPU_mem: used=11.2GB free=4.8GB
KV_cache_hits=0.68 KV_evictions=127
```

carla: KV_evictions that high on L4 is worrying. Could be fragmentation from variable-length caching + our allocator heuristic. Evictions increase recompute so latency spikes.

john: FYI T4 also shows similar behavior but threshold earlier — at ~20k tokens kernel switches. A100/H100 keep attn_v2_fused up to much larger token budgets.

raj: So two factors: 1) kernel selector chooses generic kernel for certain token-shape combos on L4/T4, 2) KV cache/allocator leads to evictions which amplify latency. We should tune per-GPU max_tokens_per_batch to avoid the selector boundary and avoid memory pressure.

maria: Quick baseline numbers I ran (p95 latency / throughput req/s) — rough: 

A10: max_tokens=48k -> p95 5.0ms / 1.8k r/s
T4: max_tokens=20k -> p95 7.9ms / 1.1k r/s
L4: max_tokens=16k -> p95 5.1ms / 1.4k r/s
A100: max_tokens=64k -> p95 3.9ms / 3.0k r/s
H100: max_tokens=72k -> p95 3.6ms / 3.4k r/s

maria: When I pushed L4 to 32k p95 jumped to 10.4ms and KV_evictions tripled.

kevin: Proposed short plan:
- Set conservative defaults: L4 16k, T4 18k, A10 48k, A100/H100 64k
- Add kernel-selector guard: prefer fused kernel when token_shape in [X..Y] by lowering threshold on L4/T4
- Adjust allocator to reserve a contiguous KV slab for long-lived sessions to reduce eviction churn (experiment flag: REDWOOD_KV_SLAB=1)
- Run 24h perf sweep with synthetic chat workload and real prompt-length distribution

raj: I support. Also add an adaptive queue policy: if queue backlog shows many similar seq lengths, allow burst-up of max_tokens for that batch (since kernels will be favorable), otherwise use conservative per-GPU ceiling. This keeps peak efficiency without regressing tails.

carla: Can we try modifying kernel selector heuristic first (cheap) and run the sweep? If that fixes most cases we can postpone allocator changes.

kevin: I'll run kernel-selector patch A and schedule sweep. Command I'm using to reproduce: 

```bash
RUNTIME_PROFILING=1 REDWOOD_KV_SLAB=0 REDWOOD_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=32768 ./run_inference_sweep.sh --gpu l4 --workload chat --duration 1h | tee l4-32k.log
```

kevin: Also collecting `kernel_selector.log` (attached to the thread) — key lines: `selected_kernel=attn_generic reason=shape_mismatch threshold=0.6`

john: quick note — for Dedicated pools we might need different defaults (customers with sustained long sessions benefit from larger slabs). Keep per-deployment overrides.

maria: I'll help analyze logs. If allocator is the culprit we should see high fragmentation in `cudaMemInfo` traces.

sre-bot: Reminder: schedule for the sweep is in eng-runtime/benchmarks calendar. Added a 2h slot tomorrow 03:00 UTC.

kevin: Thanks — will post results here. For tracking: created perf ticket PERF-824 to track kernel-selector thresholds + KV-slab experiment.

carla: :thumbsup: Let's also capture p99 and tail after changes — p95 can hide worst-case client impact.

raj: Agreed. Also add a quick micro-bench of kernel latency vs batch_shape matrix to drive selector boundaries. I can produce a heatmap.

kevin: Good. Next steps: run kernel patch, run 4 GPU-specific sweeps (T4/L4/A10/A100) overnight, share CSVs. I'll include config and logs in the ticket.

john: acked.

kevin: Closing out for now — will update thread with results.
